title: BLAKE3 4-way parallel 7-round compression kernel (256 bytes)

target_block_header.x86_64: for x86_64 needs avx needs avx512 { ... }

contract_header:
use spec = "blake3_compress_4way_spec.ode"

fn blake3_compress_4way(out: 128 bytes, cvs: 128 bytes, blocks: 256 bytes, metas: 64 bytes)
    requires no_overlap(out, cvs, blocks, metas)
    ensures out = bytes_of(spec.compress_4way(words(cvs), words(blocks), words(metas)))
    stack 256
task_summary: Implement `blake3_compress_4way(out, cvs, blocks, metas)`, which computes four independent official BLAKE3 7-round block compressions (64 bytes each, 256 bytes total) from `cvs[0..128]` (four 8-word chaining values), `blocks[0..256]` (four 16-word message blocks), and `metas[0..64]` (four 4-word `[t_lo, t_hi, length, flags]` tuples), writing the four 8-word output chaining values to `out[0..128]`. You may either use 128-bit `u32x4` SIMD (row-parallel per block, interleaved across blocks, or 4-way transposed across lanes) or 512-bit AVX-512 `u32x16` on x86-64, together with hygienic `inline fn (var ...)` helpers and `for ... unroll`. Your goal is BOTH full verification (`shown`) AND maximum throughput (lowest cycles per 256-byte call and `cyc/B`).
opt_goal: reduce total cycles per 256-byte call (and `cyc/B`) toward the vector execution-port floor (e.g., by interleaving blocks across independent vector registers, doing 4-way transposed SIMD across lanes, or using 512-bit AVX-512 `u32x16` on x86-64) while keeping `shown` verification, native tests passing, and zero unnecessary stack spills
